newsitem.title: UK: Clean tanker rates stable after brisk week.
newsitem.headline: Clean tanker rates stable after brisk week.

text.p: Chartering activity for clean product tankers was fairly brisk for most of the week but slowed towards the end with trade from the U.S. for gas oil thinning.
Last week saw a raft of gas oil fixings from the U.S. to the UK/Cont on the back of strong European gas oil, but the slight fall in prices saw trade slowing to a trickle.
A 68,000-tonne gas oil cargo was booked from the U.S. Gulf on Friday at W82.5, steady with rates for the same tonnage last week. 60kt cargoes valued steady at W100.
Interest continued to move gasoline transatlantic from Europe with a cargo booked from the Adriatic at W105.

Tanker brokers E.A. Gibson said in their weekly report that continuing delays to vessels discharging India have reduced tanker avails in the Middle East and a similar situation was being experienced in the Mediterranean due to bad weather.
They said owners operating clean vessels out of the Mediterranean were enjoying an active market with demand outstripping supply.
Naphtha fixtures were paying above W200 with suitable tonnage seen tight to the end of the month and gas oil cargo trade was also strong with 30kt cargoes taking around W170 for UKC delivery options.
